qa.question: How is Deere thinking about production versus retail by region for 2027? Given early order programs up mid-single digit, what are pricing expectations for 2027 given inflationary cost concerns?
qa.answer: Modest underproduction planned for PPA and C&F, couple percentage points  each; production plans set for full year. South America caution drives underproduction. C&F underproduction reflects continuous growth pace and four-to-five-month order position. EOP pricing rolled out to cover inflation across portfolio; focus remains on inflation coverage across PPA products as rolling toward 2027.

qa.question: Tariff expense down to $1.1 billion from $1.2 billion expected—is this due to Ag Equipment tariff relief in July or refunds? Can you explain what drove the change? Any updates on excavator launch timing and broader adoption outlook?
qa.answer: $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion driven by Section 232 tariff changes—imported goods rate dropped from  25% to 15%, effective June 1, driving five months of impact for FY 2026. Expect tailwind for FY 2027. Excavator launch occurred spring with three models now in market; positive customer feedback so far; full portfolio to roll out spring through next three-to-four years, early days with very positive reception.

qa.question: Did inventory or shipment demand slip between Q3 and Q4? Inventory-to-sales ratios show tractor inventory built in Q3. Is South America demand offset driving caution? Help understand cadence exiting year.
qa.answer: Nothing to be concerned about on inventory; shipment plans largely set for year with orders on hand. Pulled ahead  some demand in Q3 to manage risk in Q4. Factories hitting forecasts; retail pace continuing historical averages with expectations to move inventory. PPA and C&F expect similar net sales Q4 as Q3, but margins down due to no refund benefit and seasonal R&D/SA&G hits in Q4.

qa.question: Unpack early order program comments. What variability by region? Mid-single digit growth could wind up high single digits. Comment on moving pieces?
qa.answer: U.S. trending slightly better than Canada. Customers continue wanting latest technologies in planting/spraying. Best signals are mid-single digit increases in orders and doubling of See & Spray on factory sprayers and 40% of planters taking advanced technology. Confidence heading in right direction as  customers maximize everything going into 2027.

qa.question: Given EOP open for a while, what drove mid-single digit cadence of orders? Recent grain price improvement or technology decision factors?
qa.answer: Cadence as expected; made tweaks to EOP this year for dealer choice. Pleasantly surprised by tech take rates; hopeful mid-single digit increase extends through year.

qa.question: Comments on 8 Series Tractor orders aligning with EOP? Europe experiencing heat stress and input costs—how diverse are reactions? Will Europe react similarly to U.S. if crop price  response?
qa.answer: 8R orders as expected; four-to-five months out, MY2026 basically closed. Encouraged by recent commodity price changes; corn futures at $5.05 good signal for growers. Brazil three-month order book changed industry guide per circumstances. Too early for 2027. Move financing at single-digit rates hopefully drives momentum. Europe mixed: solid Small Ag & Turf but PPA exposed; arable challenged; Small Ag & Turf benefiting from dairy/livestock cash flows stable.
